checks.claim: LUT/FF and routing are separate FPGA resource classes; architecture is series-specific.
Generic HDL recommended; RTL syntax alone does not guarantee one specific CLB resource mapping.
Incomplete combinational assignment can infer an unintended latch.
Icarus uses iverilog compilation and vvp execution for Verilog simulation.
Nonblocking assignments schedule later LHS updates after RHS evaluation; clocked coding style avoids races.
7 Series devices include wide multiplexer resources; LUT mapping depends on design and tools.
Local generated clocks need suitable routing/constraints; clock enables are preferable when staying in a single domain.
Reset startup synchronization and controlled release require design-specific care.
Functional HDL simulation and testbench use iverilog plus vvp; verification must establish actual assertions.
SPI CPOL/CPHA define idle level and leading/trailing capture edges.
NXP UM10204 Rev 7 defines START/STOP, ninth ACK, clock stretching and bus clear.
24LC256 does not ACK while internal write cycle is in progress; ACK polling determines readiness rather than assuming clock stretch.
Vivado UG901 differentiates synchronous RAM inference and port read/write modes; physical collision depends on the RAM primitive.
UltraScale block memory address collisions require matching documented clock/port/mode conditions; cannot infer safe dual-clock read-first behavior.
Routing-based data path max and min delays drive setup and hold analysis.
Use recognizable CDC synchronizer circuits and ASYNC_REG attributes; report_cdc and report_synchronizer_mtbf help review.
Gray bus transfers may need max_delay -datapath_only or bus skew; check precedence of clock group exceptions.
set_input_delay and set_output_delay min/max describe external interface timing, not a local FPGA FF setup number.
Vivado 2026.1 moved to tiered licensing; BASIC remains free and supports both Windows and Linux within its tier scope.
Non-project Tcl supports read_verilog/read_xdc, synthesis, place, route, reporting and bitstream commands.
Quartus Prime QSF stores project/entity assignments while SDC stores timing constraints; project assignment precedence includes CLI, QSF, compiler database and defaults.
Quartus Prime Pro compiler supports full compilation flows including synthesis, fitter, timing analysis and programming-file generation.
TimeQuest create_clock defines clock period and targets; PLL clock derivation behavior is family/IP dependent.
Questa-Altera FPGA Starter Edition is free but requires a no-cost license for elaboration and simulation.
Questa-Altera command line supports vsim -c and vsim -do run.do invocation.
A source manifest with file hashes, device, tool version and revision aids traceability but does not itself prove bitstream reproducibility.
AXI transaction channels use VALID/READY; transfer occurs only when both are high at a rising edge and source payload stays stable until handshake.
AXI4-Lite supports single-beat 32-bit or 64-bit memory-mapped accesses and does not support burst or exclusive accesses.
MicroBlaze V is a configurable RISC-V processor with separate instruction/data interfaces and supports LMB, AXI4/AXI4-Lite and AXI4-Stream interfaces.
MicroBlaze V embedded design flow uses Vivado IP Integrator, address editor, XSA export and Vitis software platform.
Xil_Out32 writes a 32-bit value to a specified memory-mapped address.
Nios V has its own Platform Designer and software developer workflow; it should not be conflated with MicroBlaze V.
Platform Designer supports Avalon MM/Streaming, AXI, AXI-Lite, AXI-Stream and APB interfaces and generates interconnect to bridge protocol differences.
Vivado IP Packager documents AXI signal inference, clock/reset interfaces, constraints, dependencies, and IP version/revision management.

limitations: Code simulation does not establish board-level timing.
Proposed FPGA logic and timing figures are conceptual; no hardware measurements are claimed.
No synthesis resource usage, power or Fmax benchmark is asserted.
UART, SPI and I2C examples are intentionally scoped teaching units, not production protocol IP.
Chapter 14 STA numbers are arithmetic examples, not measured or Vivado-reported slack.
Chapter 15 Tcl is a guarded demonstration; no vendor build or board programming is claimed.
Chapter 16 Quartus project is generic; no board-specific pin assignment or Quartus compilation is claimed.
Chapter 17 Questa run.do is provided but public CI runs Icarus; no Questa license or simulation run is claimed.
Chapter 19 AXI4-Lite subordinate is 32-bit and single-outstanding; it is not a full AXI4 interconnect or DMA.
Chapter 20 MicroBlaze V block design is a system contract and firmware example; no board-specific XSA, ELF, bitstream or hardware run is claimed.
Build Manifest hashes input files but does not guarantee identical bitstreams across tool versions, seeds or machine environments.
Chapter 18 explains IP packaging and system integration contracts but does not claim that the sample AXI peripheral has been packaged into a vendor-specific IP archive.
